about: The layout check's configuration: the widths every page is checked at, and
each named check's thresholds under that check's own id ([[REQ-429]]).
`widths`: every check runs at every width; a finding names its width as
`tablet (900px)`. A threshold given per width name (`{ "desktop": 48,
"phone": 36 }`) applies from that width up: a width with no entry uses the
nearest smaller one (tablet uses phone's), and a screen narrower than every
entry uses the smallest.
`brand` ([[BUG-238]]): the header is the page's first section when it holds a
link. `logoMinPx` is the least height its logo image may render at.
`nameOverNav` is how much larger than the navigation links the business name
must be to read as the header's largest text. `wordmarkPx` is the size a new
site header sets the business name at ([[REQ-422]]); whatever size it ends up
at, the business name must never be smaller than the page's section headings.
`heading`: a heading belongs to the text it introduces. Spaces are measured
between the letters (their ink), not between boxes, so a display font's empty
line space counts. It is reported when the space below is at least
`belowOverAbove` times the space above (a space above under `minAbovePx` is
tight spacing, not a floating heading), and when the space below is at least
`belowOverParagraph` times the space between the text it introduces and the
next text under that — once those two are at least `minParagraphGapPx` apart,
so the lines of one list are not mistaken for paragraphs.
`table`: the cells of one row share a baseline, and the cells of one column
share a left edge, a right edge or a centre, within `tolerancePx`.
`stranded_word`: text of at least `minFontPx` running over two or more lines
with a word of at most `maxLetters` alone on a line.
`nav_wraps`: a menu link of at most `maxWords` words over more than one line.
`small_nav` and `tall_menu` apply at screens up to `maxWidthPx` wide: menu
links under `minFontPx`, and shown menu links spanning more than
`maxScreenShare` of the screen's height.
`crowded`: two controls, or a control and the header's logo or business name,
closer than `minGapPx`. `overlap`: drawn over each other by more than
`minAreaPx` square pixels.
The numbers are starting values to tune, not measurements.
